source: AIDOC-catalogued Khmer farmer leaflet, "Coconut Cultivation Techniques for Farmers" (ដំណើតកម្មដំណាំដូងសំរាប់កសិករ), prepared with NGO partners including Santi Sena, Buddhism for Development, and a farmer/agriculture association (publisher/date not fully legible on the scanned cover)
text:
Coconut (ដូង) is described as a perennial tree crop that can be grown across most regions of Cambodia. A coconut palm can live up to around 100 years and, depending on variety and growing conditions, typically begins bearing fruit around 5-7 years after planting, continuing to produce for many years afterward.

The leaflet lists the tree's wide range of uses as the reason farmers value it: the water and flesh of young nuts for drinking and eating; oil pressed from mature flesh; flesh and water used as cooking ingredients; the husk and shell burned as charcoal or used as fuel; the trunk used as timber; leaves and fiber made into brooms and roofing material; and the trunk and leaves used more broadly as house-building material.
